sam (VendorOps): Hey team — vendor Nimbus Labs sent an invoice (INV-2026-089) charging 21% IVA for digital analytics software. They say it's a foreign supplier and want us to gross-up net amount. Any precedent on Argentina VAT treatment for non-resident SaaS?
marie (Finance): Do we have their CUIT or AFIP registration? If they are foreign and not registered in AR, typically VAT on digital services can be applied to the recipient via reverse charge or taxed at source depending on service classification. Need vendor docs.
lina_nimbus (Vendor): Hi, we are a NL entity, not registered in Argentina. We billed 21% because our local partner asked. We can remove VAT if you confirm reverse charge applies and provide a statement? We prefer not to do a gross-up.
alex (Accounting): Quick checklist: 1) vendor CUIT (if any) or proof of foreign status 2) copy of contract/service description 3) confirmation whether Redwood will self-assess VAT (reverse charge) or vendor must invoice VAT. Without registration, vendor shouldn't charge AR IVA.
marie (Finance): Also need to know payment flow — is there a local reseller in AR? If payment goes to vendor abroad, AFIP rules may require withholding of certain taxes (income withholding) depending on nature of service and treaty. Do we have tax counsel about whether this is subject to withholding or just VAT reverse charge?
ivan_bot: Reminder: Please attach invoice PDF and supplier onboarding answers.
alex (Accounting): If we are to apply reverse charge, we need an internal memo stating 'Redwood Inference is the importer of services and will self-assess IVA under Art. X' (placeholder). Ops needs to record tax base and liability in ledger.
sam (VendorOps): Lina, can you ask Nimbus for: CUIT (if they ever registered), certificate of residence, and any Argentine tax registration docs? Also ask them to reissue invoice without IVA if they are not registered.
lina_nimbus (Vendor): Will request now. Also asked whether we should send a self-billing agreement.
marie (Finance): Self-billing is messy. Prefer vendor sends corrected invoice. If vendor insists on gross-up we need legal + FP approval and update PO. Gross-up calculation must be explicit: net * (1 + tax_rate) and show who bears VAT.
alex (Accounting): Practical step: hold payment until we receive either corrected invoice or formal guidance from tax counsel. Mark POs as pending tax.
sam (VendorOps): Noted. I'll pause AP action and ping vendor. ETA from vendor: EOD today.
lina_nimbus (Vendor): They replied — they don't have CUIT and say their region does not require AR registration. They propose Redwood does reverse charge and we confirm via email.
marie (Finance): OK — ask vendor for a statement of foreign status + concise service description. We'll loop in external tax advisor for Argentina specifics. If advisor says reverse charge, we'll self-assess and vendor reissues net-only invoice. If advisor says vendor must register, we'll request corrected invoice with IVA and check gross-up claim.
alex (Accounting): Action items: 1) sam to collect vendor docs 2) marie to engage tax counsel 3) accounting to block payment and flag ledger entries 4) ivan_bot to create a tax_hold tag on the invoice.
sam (VendorOps): On it. Will update thread when vendor sends docs. :thumbsup:
marie (Finance): Thanks — prefer short email trail to keep record: "Vendor X confirms non-resident; request corrected net invoicing OR provide CUIT to support charged IVA."
ivan_bot: Tax hold tag applied by AP system.
marie (Finance): Follow-up: if counsel confirms reverse charge, we'll need to record IVA liability in month of service and include it in tax reporting — accounting, please note potential GL impact.
alex (Accounting): Acknowledged. I'll prep a tentative journal template so we can plug numbers when confirmed.
sam (VendorOps): Update: vendor sent statement of non-residence and a short service description. Forwarding to marie.
marie (Finance): Received — thanks. I'll send to counsel now. Will update here once we have clearance.
sam (VendorOps): Thanks everyone.
